title: Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
summary: A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles. In particular, (acyclic) $2$-edge-coloured graphs generalize directed (acyclic) graphs (DAGs), but the complexity of problems on DAGs is much better understood than that of the corresponding problems on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs.
